answer: A shared kernel can require every agent to lock a refundable stake in a wharf contract before it may trade: the stake vests over weeks and is slashed if the agent funding trail links it to a cluster of lookalike identities. Because each fake identity costs real locked capital and time, spawning thousands of Sybils becomes unprofitable, while honest agents earn the stake back with interest. An echo of past slashing events stays public, so newcomers can verify that creating sock puppets loses money rather than gaining influence.
